title: Word Search on a Coded Grid
hints: the word must be matched in order, one grid step at a time, so this is a DFS where you only keep going if the next cell's value matches the next needed letter
try starting the search from every cell that matches word[0]

at each step, mark the current cell as visited (e.g. temporarily overwrite it with a sentinel, or use a separate visited grid), then recurse into the up/down/left/right neighbors looking for the next character

when a recursive branch fails or after you've explored all four directions, unmark the current cell (undo the visited mark) before returning - this backtrack step is essential so the same cell can be reused by a different path attempt
commonMistakes: forgetting to unmark a cell as unvisited after a failed branch, which incorrectly blocks other valid paths from reusing it
not checking board bounds before looking at a neighbor, causing an out-of-bounds access
only trying one starting cell instead of every cell that matches the first letter of the word

content.problemStatement:
You're given a grid `board` of integers, where each integer represents a letter code, and a target sequence of integers `word` representing a word (also as letter codes).

**Determine whether the word can be traced out by moving from cell to cell in the grid, where each step must move to a horizontally or vertically adjacent cell.**

No cell may be reused within a single trace.
notes: the word is longer than the number of cells in the grid (always false)
the word can be found only by a path that must resist the temptation to reuse a cell greedily
the word's first letter code does not appear anywhere in the grid (always false)

sampleTestCases.explanation: the path (0,0) -> (0,1) -> (0,2) -> (1,2) -> (2,2) spells 1,2,3,6,9 using adjacent, non-repeated cells
after reaching the 3 at (0,2), no adjacent unused cell holds the value 9
the grid only has 4 cells, so a 5-step path without reusing a cell is impossible

optimal.space: O(L) recursion depth, excluding the board itself
optimal.pattern: backtracking DFS from each matching starting cell, marking cells visited on the way down and unmarking them on the way back up

bruteForce.approach: from every cell matching word[0], try every possible sequence of adjacent moves (a full DFS tree with no early termination), checking at the end whether it spelled out the word
bruteForce.time: O(rows * cols * 4^L) where L is the word length (same order as the optimal approach, since there's no real 'brute force' shortcut for this problem)
bruteForce.space: O(L) recursion depth plus a visited-cells structure
